title: Taipei with Kids: Night Markets, Hot Springs & Day Trips
excerpt: Taipei is one of Asia's most underrated family destinations. With clean MRT, affordable attractions, incredible night market food, and natural hot springs just 30 minutes from downtown, it's perfect for families. Here's how to make the most of Taipei with kids.
author: Family Travel Asia Team
content:
Taipei is one of Asia's most underrated family travel destinations. It offers an unbeatable combination: world-class public transit that's stroller-friendly, incredibly affordable attractions, jaw-dropping night markets where kids can eat their weight in chicken cutlets and bubble tea, natural hot springs just 30 minutes from downtown, and nearby day trips that feel like a world away. Best of all, the Taiwanese genuinely adore children. Expect strangers to smile, help, and occasionally offer your kid snacks. It's a refreshingly kid-positive culture that makes traveling here a pleasure. ## Getting Around Taipei with Kids ### MRT: The Stroller-Friendly Dream The Taipei Metro (MRT) is legendary for its cleanliness, efficiency, and family-friendliness. Every station has elevators clearly signposted from street level. Trains are wide enough for strollers. Priority seats are plentiful and respected. **Cost:** Single ride NT$20–65 (US$0.60–2). Kids under 6 ride free (max 2 per paying adult). Kids 6–12 get half-price EasyCards. **EasyCard:** NT$100 (US$3) deposit, refillable at any station or convenience store. Tap for MRT, buses, and even convenience store purchases. Get one for every family member. **Stroller tip:** Avoid rush hour (8–9 AM, 6–7 PM) if possible. The MRT is so crowded during peak times that you'll struggle with a stroller. At all other times, it's easy. ## Night Markets — The Ultimate Family Feast Taipei's night markets are a highlight. They're loud, colorful, chaotic, and magical for kids. The food is cheap, safe (wash your hands after eating), and universally kid-friendly. ### 1. Shilin Night Market **📍 ** MRT Jiantan Station (Red Line), Exit 1 Taipei's largest and most famous night market. It's overwhelming but incredible for a first-timer. **Kid-friendly eats:** - **Fried chicken cutlet (ji pai)** — NT$80–100 (US$2.50–3). A huge, crispy, bone-in chicken cutlet that kids love. Get it "original" (not spicy). - **Pepper buns (hu jiao bing)** — NT$55 (US$1.70). Baked buns stuffed with pork and pepper, cooked in a traditional clay oven. A must-try. - **Taiwanese sausages** — NT$35–50 (US$1.10–1.60). Sweet, savory, on a stick. Instant kid approval. - **Oyster omelet (o-a jian)** — NT$60 (US$1.90). A local classic — mild, eggy, with a sweet sauce. - **Bubble tea (boba)** — NT$40–70 (US$1.20–2.20). You're in Taiwan. Get the real thing. **Best time to go:** 6–9 PM (before the dinner rush past 8 PM). Weekdays are quieter. **Stroller tip:** Shilin is crowded. Use a baby carrier for toddlers if possible. The market is mostly covered but the narrow aisles are tough with a stroller. ### 2. Raohe Night Market **📍** MRT Songshan Station (Green Line), Exit 5 Smaller and more manageable than Shilin, Raohe is our personal favorite for families. It's one long street — walk in one direction, eat everything, walk back. **Kid-friendly eats:** - **Hujiao bing (pepper buns)** — The original shop at the Songshan Temple entrance. NT$55 (US$1.70). - **Grilled squid** — NT$100–150 (US$3–4.60). Kids love watching it grill. - **Stinky tofu** — NT$50 (US$1.60). Yes, it smells. But adventurous kids might enjoy the fried version (less pungent). - **Tanghulu (candied fruit)** — NT$50–80 (US$1.60–2.50). Candied strawberries, grapes, or tomatoes on a stick. ### 3. Ningxia Night Market **📍** MRT Shuanglian Station (Red Line), 10-min walk The smallest of the three, but famous for authentic Taiwanese snacks. Less touristy, more local. **Must try:** The fried taro balls (NT$30 / US$0.90), roasted corn (NT$60 / US$1.90), and the legendary "Rou Yuan" (meatball soup, NT$50 / US$1.60). ### Night Market Survival Tips - Bring wet wipes. Lots of them. - Small bills only (NT$100 notes are ideal). - Vegetarian options are common. Look for "素食" (su shi) signs. - Most stalls don't have seating — you eat while walking or stand at communal tables. - Tap water is NOT drinkable. Buy bottled water or bring a refillable bottle and fill at hotel. ## Beitou Hot Springs **📍** MRT Xinbeitou Station (Red Line), 30 min from Taipei Main Station Beitou is a hot spring town nestled in the mountains, just a 30-minute MRT ride from Taipei. It's a fantastic half-day adventure with kids. ### What to Do **1. Beitou Public Hot Springs (free)** - **Location:** Near Beitou Park, just outside Xinbeitou Station - **Cost:** Free — these are foot baths on the public plaza where anyone can soak their feet in 40°C hot spring water. - **Best for:** Toddlers and young kids who just want to splash. **2. Millenium Hot Spring (public pool)** - **Cost:** NT$60 (US$1.90) for adults, half-price for children. Super cheap. - **Details:** Outdoor pools at 38–42°C, separated by gender (swimwear required in mixed areas on certain days). - **Stroller tip:** Changing rooms are basic. Bring swim diapers for toddlers. **3. Hot Spring Hotels (private rooms)** If you want a private family experience, book a 90-minute soak at one of Beitou's famous hotels: - **Spring City Resort** — Family bath from NT$1,500 (US$46), has children's play area. - **Grand View Resort** — Private hot spring rooms from NT$1,200 (US$37) for 90 min. **Other Beitou attractions:** - **Beitou Hot Springs Museum** (free) — A beautiful Japanese-era bathhouse, now a museum. Free entry. - **Thermal Valley** — A steaming, turquoise-green hot spring that's 90°C. Walk the path around it (free). Kids are mesmerized by the steam. - **Geothermal Hell Valley** — More dramatic steam vents and hot springs. Free. ## Taipei Zoo & Maokong Gondola **📍** MRT Taipei Zoo Station (Brown Line) One of the largest zoos in Asia, and one of the cheapest. **Cost:** NT$60 (US$1.90) for adults. Children under 6 enter FREE. Yes, you read that right — the whole family can enter for under $2. **Highlights:** - **Panda House** — Home to giant pandas Tuan Tuan and Yuan Yuan and their cubs. - **Koala House** — Cute Australian export. - **Insectarium** — Interactive bug exhibits kids love. - **Children's Zoo** — Petting area with goats, rabbits, and guinea pigs. - **Formosan Animal Area** — Native Taiwanese species like the Formosan black bear. **Maokong Gondola:** Right next to the zoo entrance, the gondola takes you up into the hills for panoramic views of Taipei. The Glass Floor cabins (with see-through floors) are a thrill for kids. **Cost:** NT$120 (US$3.70) one way, NT$240 (US$7.40) round trip. Under 6 free. **At Maokong:** Enjoy tea houses (Taiwan's famous oolong tea), hike the tea trails, or visit the Zhinan Temple. Many tea houses serve simple noodle dishes and tea eggs — perfect for a family lunch. ## Day Trips from Taipei ### 1. Jiufen (Half-Day) **📍** 1 hour by bus from Taipei The mountain town that inspired Studio Ghibli's "Spirited Away." A maze of narrow alleys, red lanterns, tea houses, and incredible mountain views. **Cost:** Bus NT$90 (US$2.80) one way. Free to walk the old street. **Kid-friendly eats:** - **Taro balls** — NT$50 (US$1.60). Chewy, sweet, purple balls in syrup. - **Fish ball soup** — NT$60 (US$1.90). Mild and kid-approved. - **Peanut ice cream rolls** — NT$50 (US$1.60). Shaved peanut candy wrapped around ice cream and cilantro. Sounds weird, tastes amazing. **Stroller tip:** Jiufen's main street is steps and narrow alleys. **Leave the stroller at the hotel** and use a baby carrier. Your shoulders will thank you. ### 2. Yehliu Geopark (Half-Day) **📍** 40 min by bus from Taipei Otherworldly rock formations along the coast, formed by millennia of wind and water erosion. The "Queen's Head" rock is the most famous. **Cost:** NT$120 (US$3.70), under 6 free. **Kid appeal:** Running around the huge rock formations, watching waves crash, and "discovering" shapes in the rocks. Best for ages 3+ who can follow safety rules (no climbing on the fragile formations). **Stroller tip:** The path is paved but uneven. A sturdy stroller with larger wheels works; umbrella strollers struggle on the gravel. ### 3. Taichung & Sun Moon Lake (Full Day or Overnight) **📍** 1 hour by high-speed rail from Taipei Taiwan's central city and its beautiful lake. Take the HSR to Taichung (NT$700 / US$22 one way, 1 hour), then a bus to Sun Moon Lake (NT$160 / US$5, 90 min). **Cost:** HSR round trip ~$44 per adult. Sun Moon Lake boat tour NT$300 (US$9.30). **Kid-friendly activities:** - **Sun Moon Lake bike path** — One of the world's most beautiful cycling routes. Rent family bikes (NT$200–400 / US$6–12 per hour) or e-bikes. - **Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village** (NT$850 / US$26 per adult, kids 6–12 NT$750 / US$23) — Amusement park + indigenous culture show. ## Where to Stay in Taipei with Kids | Area | Best For | Example Hotel | Price/Night | |------|----------|---------------|-------------| | **Ximending** | Night markets, shopping, convenient MRT | Hotel Papa Whale | $50–80 | | **Taipei Main Station** | Transport hub, easiest connections | Palais de Chine | $100–180 | | **Da'an District** | Upscale, quieter, near parks | Mandarin Oriental | $250–400 | | **Beitou** | Hot springs, relaxation | Grand View Resort | $120–200 | **Budget pick:** **Ximen Citizen Hotel** (~$45–65/night) — clean, family rooms, 2-min walk to Ximending shops and night market. Breakfast included. ## Sample 4-Day Taipei Itinerary **Day 1: Arrival + Night Market Intro** - Arrive, check into Ximending hotel - Evening: Raohe Night Market (easy, manageable, delicious) **Day 2: Zoo + Gondola** - Morning: Taipei Zoo (arrive when it opens at 9 AM, see pandas first) - Lunch: Maokong tea houses (try the Tieguanyin oolong + simple noodles) - Afternoon: Maokong Gondola back down, rest at hotel - Evening: Shilin Night Market (the big one) **Day 3: Hot Springs + Old Taipei** - Morning: Beitou hot springs (foot bath + Thermal Valley) - Lunch: Beitou market street (cheap noodles and dumplings) - Afternoon: Taipei 101 (observatory NT$600 / US$18.50 adult, kids under 6 free — or skip and just see it from below for free) - Evening: Din Tai Fung (Xiao long bao — get the original pork, NT$230 / US$7 for 10 pieces) **Day 4: Day Trip** - Jiufen (half-day) or Yehliu (half-day) - Afternoon: Last-minute shopping, Ximending arcades for kids - Depart ## Budget Summary for a Family of 4 | Item | Cost (USD) | |------|-----------| | MRT (3 days, 2 adults) | $12 | | Taipei Zoo (2 adults) | $3.80 | | Maokong Gondola (2 adults) | $7.40 each way | | Night market dinner (family) | $15–25 | | Beitou foot bath | FREE | | Private hot spring (90 min) | $35–50 | | Jiufen bus (2 adults) | $5.60 each way | | Din Tai Fung dinner (family) | $25–40 | | **Total for 4 days per family** | **~$350–550** | Taipei is proof that a world-class family vacation doesn't need to break the bank. With its incredible food, welcoming culture, and easy access to nature and hot springs, it's a city the whole family will fall in love with.
